title: Brute Force + Suspicious PowerShell + Possible Exfiltration
mitre_techniques: T1110 - Brute Force; T1059.001 - PowerShell; Potential exfiltration behavior
analyst_rationale: Multiple authentication failures were followed by successful authentication, suspicious PowerShell execution and abnormal outbound transfer activity.
recommended_investigation: Validate authentication; investigate source IP; review PowerShell command line; investigate outbound destination; search for related events across the environment.

title: Impossible Travel Authentication Pattern
analyst_rationale: Successful authentication events associated with geographically inconsistent locations within a short time window require validation of account legitimacy.
recommended_investigation: Validate account activity, authentication location and device.

title: Potential SMB Lateral Movement
mitre_techniques: T1021.002 - SMB/Windows Admin Shares; Potential lateral movement
analyst_rationale: A single internal source communicated with multiple internal systems over SMB, which can indicate lateral movement.
recommended_investigation: Review SMB connections, source host activity and contacted systems for lateral movement indicators.

title: Abnormal Outbound Data Transfer
mitre_techniques: Potential T1041 - Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
analyst_rationale: Outbound data volume materially exceeds the normal profile assumed for the simulated environment and requires destination and file-level investigation.
recommended_investigation: Investigate destination, transferred data and user/device baseline before determining whether exfiltration occurred.

title: Office-to-PowerShell Process Chain
analyst_rationale: A document application spawned command execution followed by PowerShell with an encoded command, representing a high-risk endpoint execution chain.
recommended_investigation: Review document origin, child-process chain, PowerShell command line and endpoint activity.
